## Verdict

missing

## Bearer

ConnectivityPermissionSystem — core-domain/src/main/kotlin/com/mgilli/core/domain/connectivity/ConnectivityPermissionSystem.kt

## Trigger

ConnectivityPermissionManager.onLaunch and ConnectivityPermissionManager.requestAgain, both in core-domain/src/main/kotlin/com/mgilli/core/domain/connectivity/ConnectivityPermissionManager.kt — observed

## Today

ConnectivityPermissionSystem is an interface only — `isGranted()`,
`canShowSystemPrompt()`, `requestPermission()`, `openAppSettings()` —
its doc comment stating explicitly that a real-OS-backed
implementation is not part of the lot that created it.
ConnectivityPermissionManager already calls all four methods
(`onLaunch()` calls `requestPermission()`/`isGranted()`,
`requestAgain()` calls `canShowSystemPrompt()`/`requestPermission()`/
`openAppSettings()`), so the calling side is complete. The only
callers of `ConnectivityPermissionSystem` anywhere in the code are
`ConnectivityPermissionManager` and the fakes used in
`ProfileViewModelTest`, `ProfileScreenTest`,
`ConnectivityPermissionManagerTest` and `HomeViewModelTest`; no class
implements it against a real Android permission API. Which OS
permission the interface stands for has not been decided anywhere in
the code: no permission string, no `Manifest.permission.*` reference,
no `BLUETOOTH_CONNECT`/companion-device reference exists in either
application module. `ConnectivityPermissionManager` is used from both
`app-phone` (`ProfileViewModel`) and `app-wear` (`HomeViewModel`), so
the OS-backed behaviour differs by side — the phone reaches a paired
watch, the watch reaches a paired phone — while the interface itself
carries no Android import and can stay in `:core-domain` as the
shared contract, per the module-split convention that a platform
adapter touching OS permissions lives in the application module using
it (§3 of the conventions). The sibling case, `SensorPermissionSystem`
(app-wear only), follows that same split today: its interface and its
still-unimplemented real form both sit in `app-wear`, confirming the
pattern an implementation of `ConnectivityPermissionSystem` would
follow — one instance per application module, each choosing the OS
permission call that fits its side.

## Expected

Each application module — `app-phone` and `app-wear` — holds a
concrete implementation of `ConnectivityPermissionSystem`, backed by
a decided OS permission that stands for reaching the paired device
(the choice is part of this fix, not made yet in either module).
`isGranted()` reads the current state of that permission with no
prompt shown; `canShowSystemPrompt()` reports whether the OS will
still show its own dialog for it; `requestPermission()` triggers that
system dialog and suspends for the resolution; `openAppSettings()`
opens the app's own page in the system settings. Both
implementations are reachable by `ConnectivityPermissionManager`,
which already calls all four members from `onLaunch()` and
`requestAgain()`.
